snippet.title: FrameMaker Essentials - Mastering conditional text for smarter content delivery
snippet.description:
Managing multiple versions of content is one of the biggest challenges for documentation teams. Whether it's product editions, regional variations, or audience‑specific instructions, authors often struggle to maintain consistency and avoid duplicate work.

In this webinar, Barb Binder will walk you through how Adobe FrameMaker’s powerful conditional text capabilities help you streamline authoring, simplify version management, and deliver cleaner, more relevant content to every end user.

You will learn how to:
• Manage multiple content versions from a single source using conditional tags.
• Keep documentation consistent by quickly auditing and cleaning tag usage.
• Standardize conditional tagging across teams for reliable version control.
• Instantly preview what each audience or output will see before publishing.
• Deliver clear, relevant, audience specific content every time.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

snippet.title: ADW26-D3-S09 – The Content Space Bar – Stefan Gentz, Bernard Aschwanden and Guests
snippet.description:
After Hour: The Future of Content — Stefan Gentz, Principal Worldwide Evangelist for Technical Communication at Adobe

Hosts:
- Stefan Gentz, Principal Worldwide Evangelist at Adobe
- Bernard Aschwanden, CEO at WritemoreAI

Guests:

- Janine Trakthenberg (Hashout)
- Ed Marsh (Ex-Goldman Sachs VP)
- Sebastian Fuhrer (Mayo Clinic)
- Andrea Ames (Idyll Point™ Group)
- Jack Molisani (LavaCon=

About this Session:

Forget the slides. Forget the polished demos. Forget the “safe” conference answers.

As DITAWORLD 2026 comes to a close, join Stefan Gentz and Bernard Aschwanden for a completely different kind of session — part industry therapy, part late-night talk, part unfiltered reality check on the future of content.

Inspired by the atmosphere of after-hours bar conversations at conferences, this session brings together industry veterans, thought leaders, and surprise guests for an honest, witty, and occasionally provocative discussion about technical communication, AI, structured content, enterprise chaos, and everything in between.

Expect stories from the trenches. Hard truths. Nostalgic throwbacks. Hot takes. Moments of disagreement. And probably a few things nobody was supposed to say out loud.

From “DITA is dead” debates to AI hype cycles, from content governance nightmares to the future of dynamic, intelligent experiences — nothing is off the table.

No scripts. No corporate polish. No marketing theater.

Just smart people, real conversations, and one final drink before the lights go out on DITAWORLD 2026.

Come for the laughs. Stay for the uncomfortable accuracy.

Conference website: https://2026-adobe-dita-world.meetus.adobeevents.com/

snippet.title: [ADW26-D1-S08] The Future of Content (and Content Professionals!) – Hosted by LavaCon
snippet.description:
The Future of Content (and Content Professionals!)

Host:

- Jack Molisani, Executive Director, LavaCon

Panelists:

- Aman Goyal, T-Mobile
- Josh Steves, International Risk Management Institute, Inc.
- Noz Urbina, Urbina Consulting


About this Session:

AI is changing more than the tools we use—it is redefining how content is created, managed, discovered, delivered, and consumed. As generative and agentic AI become part of everyday business workflows, content professionals face a fundamental question:

What role will humans play in the future of content?

Join LavaCon founder and industry veteran Jack Molisani for a thought-provoking panel discussion featuring three leading voices at the intersection of content strategy, AI, knowledge management, and customer experience.

Aman Goyal brings firsthand experience building agentic AI systems and enterprise-scale knowledge platforms at T-Mobile. Josh Steves shares practical insights from two decades of content architecture and AI-driven content operations. Noz Urbina, one of the industry’s foremost experts on omnichannel content and customer experience, offers a strategic perspective on how AI is reshaping not only content ecosystems but also the relationship between organizations and their audiences.

Together, they will explore how AI is changing the content profession, what new skills organizations will need, and how content teams can evolve from content creators to orchestrators of knowledge, experiences, and intelligent systems.

Whether you are excited, skeptical, or somewhere in between, this session will challenge assumptions, spark new ideas, and help you prepare for the next chapter of content strategy.

Key Takeaways:

- The future of content creation: Understand how generative and agentic AI are changing content workflows and production models.
- The evolution of content roles: Learn which skills will become more valuable—and which may become less relevant—in an AI-powered workplace.
- Content as knowledge infrastructure: Discover why structured, connected, and trustworthy content is becoming the foundation for AI-driven experiences.
- The future of customer experience: Explore how AI is transforming search, discovery, personalization, and content consumption.
- Preparing for what’s next: Gain practical insights on how content professionals can remain relevant, influential, and indispensable in the years ahead.

snippet.title: [ADW26-D3-S08] Managing DITA Profiles in AEM Guides — Getting ready for DITA 2.0 (Steinbacher)
snippet.description:
Managing DITA Profiles in AEM Guides — Getting ready for DITA 2.0 and more!

Speaker:

- Leroy Steinbacher, Senior Solutions Consultant at Adobe

About this Session:

As DITA evolves toward version 2.0 and organizations increasingly adopt customized vocabularies, specialization, and non-standard output pipelines, managing DITA infrastructure becomes a critical capability—not an afterthought.

In this technical deep-dive, you’ll learn how to configure and manage DITA Profiles in Adobe Experience Manager Guides to support both standard and customized DITA environments. The session walks through uploading and maintaining catalog files, DTDs, schemas, and constraints using the AEM Guides DITA Profile tool, enabling teams to control exactly which DITA constructs are available to authors.

You’ll also see how to download, install, and integrate the DITA Open Toolkit (DITA-OT)—including custom plugins—into AEM Guides to support specialized output formats, publishing pipelines, and future-ready transformations. Along the way, we’ll discuss practical considerations for versioning, governance, and migration as organizations prepare for DITA 2.0 while continuing to support existing DITA 1.x content.

This session is ideal for architects, advanced implementers, and anyone responsible for keeping their DITA ecosystem scalable, compliant, and future-proof.

Key Takeaways:

- How DITA Profiles work in AEM Guides and when to use them
- Uploading and managing catalogs, DTDs, schemas, and constraints
- Best practices for controlling authoring environments via profiles
- Installing and configuring the DITA Open Toolkit in AEM Guides
- Integrating custom DITA-OT plugins for specialized outputs
- Preparing your content and tooling strategy for DITA 2.0
- Governance and migration considerations for mixed DITA environments

Event website: https://2026-adobe-dita-world.meetus.adobeevents.com/

snippet.title: [ADW26-D3-S07] Accessible by Design — How to Create DITA Content That Works for Everyone (Johnson)
snippet.description:
Accessible by Design — How to Create DITA Content That Works for Everyone

Speaker:

- Bob Johnson, Content Strategy Consultant

About this Session:

Accessibility is no longer optional—it is an essential part of delivering effective, inclusive, and compliant content experiences. As accessibility regulations continue to evolve and organizations strive to serve diverse audiences, technical communicators play a critical role in ensuring that information is accessible to everyone.

In this session, accessibility expert Bob Johnson provides a practical introduction to accessibility in technical communication and structured content. He will explore common types of disabilities, explain why accessibility matters for both users and organizations, and demystify key standards such as the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

Drawing on years of hands-on experience with DITA and accessibility initiatives, Bob will share practical guidance for creating, managing, and publishing accessible DITA content. Whether you are just beginning your accessibility journey or looking to strengthen existing practices, this session will help you build a stronger foundation for inclusive content delivery.

Key Takeaways:

- Understand accessibility fundamentals: Learn how different disabilities can affect the way users consume technical content.
- Navigate accessibility standards: Gain a practical understanding of WCAG and its relevance to technical communication.
- Apply accessibility in DITA: Discover techniques and best practices for creating accessible structured content.
- Reduce risk and improve user experience: See how accessibility supports compliance, usability, and broader audience reach.

snippet.description:
It’s Not Magic. It’s Metadata! Aligning Content Strategy to Business Outcomes

Speaker:

- Amber Swope, DITA Specialist, DITA Strategies, Inc.

About this Session:

Content leaders are under increasing pressure to deliver measurable impact—faster publishing, lower costs, better customer experiences. Yet many DITA and AEM implementations fall short, not because of tools, but because of weak or misaligned metadata strategies.

Join Amber Swope to explore how metadata acts as the critical link between structured content and business results and learn how your metadata strategy can enable governance, power automation, and provide the insights needed to demonstrate value.

Key Takeaway:

- Metadata isn’t just structure—it’s how content strategy becomes business strategy

snippet.title: [ADW26-D3-S04] Thomson Reuters’ Human-Guided Approach to AI Content (Byrnes, Enneking)
snippet.description:
Writing at Scale, Intentionally — Thomson Reuters’ Human-Guided Approach to AI Content

Speakers:

- Holly Enneking, VP of Marketing at markup.ai
- Emily Byrnes, Senior Manager of Content Strategy at Thomson Reuters

About this Session:

A team of 10 writers. 200+ products. And a mandate to do more with AI — without letting AI drive.

In this session, Emily Byrnes, Senior Manager of Content Strategy at Thomson Reuters, joins Markup AI to share how her Help & Support content team is navigating the reality of AI-assisted content creation: where it earns a seat in the workflow, where it doesn't, and how writers are empowered to make that call themselves.

You'll hear how the team uses LLMs to ideate and draft, AEM Guides to publish, and Markup AI to ensure every piece of content that ships is fully on-brand — because they've learned that AI doesn't do that part well on its own.

If you're leading a content team that's being asked to scale without sacrificing quality, this is the session for you.

snippet.title: KDP University @home with Michaelbrent Collings
snippet.description:
Novelist and  screenwriter Michaelbrent Collings is one of the most successful indie horror authors in the US, as well as an international best-selling thriller, fantasy, science fiction, and mystery writer. His works have been nominated for Bram Stoker, Dragon, and RONE awards.
Collings is a frequent guest at comic cons and writing podcasts like Six Figure Authors, The Creative Penn, Writing Excuses, and more. 
On October 28, Collings shared with us how writing helped him gain a whole new sense of hope and how branding and event attendance can build your readership.

snippet.title: KDP University @home with Andrew Watts
snippet.description: In 2012, while deployed on a USS Navy aircraft carrier, Andrew Watts took up writing as a way to occupy his free time. Fast-forward nearly a decade and Watts is now the owner of Severn River Publishing, which has published titles for over 20 authors. Drawing on his experience in the military and working in brand management for one of the world’s largest consumer-goods companies, Watts uses his discipline and marketing acumen to turn his projects into reality as a successful author and business owner. On September 2, Watts joined us to share his top tips for starting and growing your career as an indie author—from his unique perspective on both sides of the pen.

snippet.title: Setting Up Media Storage in DaVinci Resolve
snippet.description:
Watch this short video to learn how to set up your media storage location in DaVinci Resolve. This lets you define your scratch disk, additional media storage locations, proxy locations and default cache directories for new projects.

Setting up these locations correctly helps keep your media, proxies and cache files organized, improves performance when working with high resolution footage, and makes it easier to manage storage across internal drives, external disks or shared storage. It also helps ensure new projects are set up consistently from the start, reducing the chance of missing media, full drives or files being saved in the wrong location.

The latest version of DaVinci Resolve can be downloaded from https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve.

There’s also support for full screen portrait mode HDMI output, front camera support for portrait and landscape orientations without rotation on iPhone 17.

Blackmagic Camera for iOS 3.3 is available now as a free download from

snippet.title: Backing Up Media with the Clone Tool in DaVinci Resolve
snippet.description:
Watch this short video to learn how to back up your media and use checksum verification with the Clone Tool. Creating copies of your original media files and storing them on separate drives helps protect your footage, while checksum verification ensures your backups match the source files and have not been corrupted during transfer or storage.
 
The latest version of DaVinci Resolve can be downloaded from https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve.

snippet.title: How I Made This Stylized Glowing Honey Jar in Blender
snippet.description:
Follow along to see how Kenny models, shades, lights, composites, and renders a glowing stylized honey jar in Blender, start to finish. Kenny walks through the whole scene from an empty file: the glass jar, the honey inside, the cork, the drips, a custom label, and the final animated render.

This is a perfect 2nd Blender project if you've taken the Blender Donut tutorial. 

Grab the project files (free): https://honeyjar.cgcookie.com

This one scene touches five disciplines. If you want to go deeper on any of them, they're each a full course in CORE, our Blender fundamentals series rebuilt for Blender 5.2: https://core.cgcookie.com

The CG Cookie challenge: make your own jarred product. Swap the label, change the color, tweak the details, then tag us and we'll repost our favorites.

localized.description:
Follow along to see how Kenny models, shades, lights, composites, and renders a glowing stylized honey jar in Blender, start to finish. Kenny walks through the whole scene from an empty file: the glass jar, the honey inside, the cork, the drips, a custom label, and the final animated render.

This is a perfect 2nd Blender project if you've taken the Blender Donut tutorial. 

Grab the project files (free): https://honeyjar.cgcookie.com

This one scene touches five disciplines. If you want to go deeper on any of them, they're each a full course in CORE, our Blender fundamentals series rebuilt for Blender 5.2: https://core.cgcookie.com

The CG Cookie challenge: make your own jarred product. Swap the label, change the color, tweak the details, then tag us and we'll repost our favorites.

snippet.title: Procedural Parallax Effect in Blender
snippet.description:
Learn how to create a procedural parallax effect using shader nodes in this Blender tutorial. Parallax mapping is a technique used to give a 2 dimensional surface a truly 3 dimensional look. It's different than bump mapping and normal mapping because parallax mapping creates the illusion of depth, not just surface detail. And this depth is based on the perspective too, creating a convincing 3 dimensional feel from every angle. This shader was originally made for this tutorial by Erindale Woodford. Check out more of his work here - https://linktr.ee/erindale.xyz

Download the project files here -
https://cgmasters.com/tutorials/parallax.zip

snippet.title: Master Procedural Texturing in Blender | Out Now!
snippet.description:
Check it out here - https://www.blendermarket.com/products/master-procedural-texturing-in-blender

Tap into the unlimited potential of Blender’s incredibly powerful node editor, and learn how to create advanced and highly customizable procedural textures from scratch. In this course I’ll walk you through building complex textures, step by step. You’ll learn about a ton of different nodes and creative ways you can combine them to achieve amazing results.

We’ll focus on two big projects in this course, highly customizable Subway Tiles and an animated and customizable Lava Field. Both are fun and complex projects that will give us a good mix of both technical and organic styles of textures.

For this course I teamed up with procedural texture master Erindale Woodford. Erin created the textures and I created the training. We chose these specific topics to focus on important texture building skills like technical planning and texture layering to help you gain a strong understanding of how to approach and achieve complexity.

snippet.title: Blender for Complete and Total Beginners
snippet.description:
Blender for Complete and Total Beginners is the best starting point for anyone interested in learning 3D and Blender. Check out the course page to learn more - https://cgmasters.com/blender-for-complete-and-total-beginners/

Blender is perfect for anyone interested in learning 3D, because it’s incredibly powerful and free. This full creation suite offers a complete range of artistic possibilities, including modeling, animation, rendering, compositing, video editing, and a lot more. So whether you’re interested in creating games, producing animations, 3D printing, or anything else related to 3D, Blender has you covered with it’s complete production toolkit.

Learning such an advanced piece of software can be intimidating though. There are a crazy amount of tools and it can be tricky to figure out where to start. That’s what this course is for. This curriculum was designed to give you a clear understanding of the most fundamental concepts and tools, even if you have zero experience.

snippet.title: De-mudding the low end with Melodyne
snippet.description:
Working on the low end of a bass sound is all about choosing the right tools. Traditional EQs can certainly de-mud sounds, but at the cost of reducing the instrument's weight or power.
Let Sensho show you better alternatives: One option is the formant tool, which is part of Melodyne assistant or higher. Or, if you have Melodyne studio, you can shift smaller bands of formants and combine this with sophisticated leveling of overtones. This allows the bass example in this video to take on different sound characters while always staying well balanced and ready to fit in the mix.

Try it out for yourself with all your bass sounds, as well as any other track that could benefit from more clarity and weight.

snippet.title: Tonalic Instrument: Julian Coryell's Tele Deluxe
snippet.description:
Julian Coryell was raised in the "family business" as his father is the famous guitar player Larry Coryell and he started to play guitar when he was very young. He attended Berklee and becoming the college's youngest graduate then. Later, he played live with Alanis Morissette, Jewel, Aimee Mann and many more.

In this video, Julian talks about the unique character of the Tele Deluxe, a Fender guitar developed in collaboration with Seth Lover from Gibson. With a Gibson-style scale length and Seth Lover pickups, it delivers a warmer, fuller tone than a traditional Telecaster, perfect for pop, arpeggiated parts, and gritty lead sounds inspired by Keith Richards. The guitar’s versatility and sparkly warmth make it Julian's go-to choice for sessions and live work. 

--

No AI, no loops, no MIDI. Just a musician playing along to every chord, every tempo, every groove. Effortlessly.

snippet.description:

snippet.description:

snippet.title: 2025 Core77 Design Awards Autodesk Fusion Prize
snippet.description:

snippet.title: You Touch, You Buy.
snippet.description:
For the first time since 2017, I recorded the process behind one of my artworks. Much of what you can see in this short film was broadcasted live on Twitch. It shows my interpretation of Bobs workplace plus additional pieces that highlight the sticky and moldy nature of his business. Everything’s been touched before, nothing is new. Mint condition, but not really.

Thanks, love, praise & eternal glory goes out to:
Jasmin Dämmrich, Alex Rych, Raphael Rau, Lukas Guziel, Ash Thorp, Billy Chitkin, Jeremy Cox, Dino Muhic and literally hundreds of people who were constantly cheering and supporting me with their knowledge, kindness and love during long days of streaming. I would love to make a list with all your names, but I can’t, because you were so many. I will never forget you though.

The project would not have been possible without the help of RNDR.

snippet.title: Learn GIMP 3.0 Photo Editing for Beginners in 25 Minutes
snippet.description:
Learn how to edit photos from start to finish in GIMP 3.0, the free photo editor and photoshop alternative! This tutorial walks you through a simple yet effective 10 step process for creating AWESOME photos EVERY TIME! From adjusting exposure and shadows-highlights, to enhancing colors with levels and saturation, to adding contrast with curves, to sharpening and denoising, to cropping and exporting - I cover every important detail as a total beginner you need to know to edit great photos consistently. 

No Adobe subscription required! The GNU Image Manipulation Program is totally free and open source.

0:00 - Intro
0:20 - Step 0: Import a Photo
0:43 - Step 1: Exposure
3:44 - GIMP 3.0 Layer Effects
4:22 - Step 2: Shadows-Highlights
7:59 - How to Save Your Work
8:18 - Step 3: Levels

snippet.title: GIMP's Future After GIMP 3.0: What's Next
snippet.description:
Now that GIMP 3.0 has been released, what can we expect in the future for the GIMP project? In this video, I discuss news around GIMP development, including features expected in GIMP 3.2 like smart objects and vector layers! Plus, I discuss other exciting features on GIMP's radar like a vector Shape tool, full CMYK support, animation features, a built-in "inpainting" tool (from the Resynthesizer plug), and more!

Additionally, I cover a Libre Arts article that discusses GIMP's approx. $2 million in Bitcoin, which it began liquidating for cash through the Gnome Foundation. Will GIMP start hiring paid developers to implement awesome new features?

snippet.title: A new animation technique ! Bringing the 2d timing chart to 3d (Blender Add-on)
snippet.description:
A new animation tool for #blender3d ! Developper by me and Samuel Bernou.
You can get it here : https://dedouze.gumroad.com/l/fsbdw
Update : New feature added, check part 2 here : https://youtu.be/6t5NvcByqNg

This add-on brings together the fun of 2d animation and the power of 3D ! You can simply draw the trajectory of your Object/Bone, trace the spacings you want on that trajectory, and then press « Animate », and voilà, you just generated an animation !

I already showed a beta version of this tool a few months ago. Now it’s working perfectly ! Thanks for your support!! 🙏🙏🌸

snippet.title: A Case Study of Wikimedia for DPLA institutions
snippet.description:
The Wikipedia for Cultural Heritage lecture series will end with a case study from a DPLA hub, the Minnesota Digital Library. Working together with a cohort of several of their contributing institutions, including Hennepin County Library, MDL utilized the DPLA Wikimedia pipeline to share over 700,000 images. Sara Ring, one of the project’s coordinators, and Bailey Diers, project participant, will offer an overview of how they got started in their work on Wikipedia, how it has been going, and offer insights into how an institution could start their own project.

Speakers:
Sara Ring, Continuing Education Librarian, Minitex
Bailey Diers, Special Collections Librarian, Hennepin County Library

snippet.title: Wikipedia Metrics & Tools for DPLA Contributors
snippet.description: With Christine Fernsebner Eslao, Giovanna Fontenelle, and Jamie Flood. Join members of the Wikimedia Working for an overview of metrics and tracking tools across Wikimedia platforms. We will look at metrics and tools while offering advice for institutions currently contributing, or looking to get involved with the DPLA Wikimedia Pipeline, and related Wikipedia work and editing. During the presentation we will cover pipeline metrics, Wikimedia events dashboard and using it for tracking, article assessment tools, a tool for adding images to articles, and Wikimedia Commons specific tools. Additionally, we will briefly discuss new Wikimedia Foundation tools that are being developed. The presenters have first hand experience with all tools being covered and will offer insight and demonstrations into how to best utilize them for your personal or institutional editing and content goals.

snippet.title: Wikipedia Edit-a-thons: Minimum Lift for Maximum Reward
snippet.description: While Wikipedia edit-a-thons may sound like a daunting event opportunity, sharing experiences, guides, and best practices, can make editing an easy engagement opportunity for institutions contributing to Wikimedia Commons through DPLA. Jamie Flood has been organizing and supporting Wikipedia editing events for almost a decade, and has worked the process of organizing an event into an accessible, if not easy, opportunity to engage community members with cultural heritage collections. During the presentation, we will look at different event types/styles, how to handle a work list and tracking, and best practices for outreach to ensure you meet interested community members – and even experienced Wikipedians.

snippet.title: Assessing Opportunities for Engagement with the Wikipedia Workbook for Cultural Institutions
snippet.description:
Featuring Mary Mark Ockerbloom. The “Wikipedia Workbook for Cultural Institutions” is designed to help Wikipedians, Wikimedians in Residence and interested GLAM institutions (Galleries, Libraries, Archives, Museums) to survey opportunities for engagement with Wikipedia and its related projects. The Workbook gives an overview of key projects, the ways in which they can and cannot be used, and where to find resources to learn more about using them. Both Wikipedians and GLAM professionals have specialized knowledge and skills. This Workbook attempts to introduce key concepts and information that will be useful to both groups and support more rewarding conversations and collaborations.

The Workbook is organized so that it pairs information with suggested tasks. You can focus on the content that is most useful to you. Major sections include: Using this workbook, Wikipedia articles, Wikimedia Commons, Wikidata, Logic models and metrics, Institutional workflows, and a bibliography of Resources. Sections include topics such as OpenRefine, InteGraality, and dealing with disinformation. The intention is not to teach someone everything they may need to know; rather, it gives starting points for further exploration. The Workbook can help Wikimedians and GLAM partners to assess their resources, identify areas where they can potentially contribute, define their goals, and plan ways to measure their impact.

The Wikipedia Workbook for Cultural Institutions was developed with support from Vizcaya Museum and Gardens in Miami, Florida, and is freely available on Wikimedia Commons.

snippet.title: Leveraging the Decentralized Web to Preserve Cultural Heritage
snippet.description:
As part of our ongoing effort to serve as a bridge between our institutional partners and emerging technologies, DPLA has started to explore the benefits of decentralized storage. Long-term storage on the decentralized web is one approach to ensuring the protection of cultural artifacts and heritage — against both natural and man-made threats, such as natural disasters, loss of funding, or technological failures. In this webinar, we will share the results of a pilot project to upload some of our partner content onto Filecoin’s decentralized storage network. During the webinar, we will be joined by speakers from the Filecoin Foundation for the Decentralized Web (FFDW) to help the DPLA community understand  decentralized storage technology and how they can leverage it for added resilience.

Speaker:
Jefferson Sankara is a Senior Software Product Engineer at the Filecoin Foundation, where he leads the development of Singularity—the only open-source, end-to-end data onboarding platform for the Filecoin network. With over a decade of experience in product management, data science, machine learning, and blockchain technology, he specializes in creating tools that empower organizations to preserve, discover, and derive long-term value from decentralized storage networks. In this webinar, Sankara will share insights on how libraries can leverage filecoin’s decentralized storage solutions to preserve data securely and reliably. His unique blend of product strategy, technical expertise, and passion for decentralized systems makes him an invaluable voice for libraries exploring Web3 technologies.

snippet.title: DPLA Hub Spotlight: The New Michigan Memories
snippet.description:
Join us as we spotlight the recent relaunch of Michigan Memories, a website that allows users to search the online collections of cultural institutions all around the state. Michigan Memories is the Michigan-centric counterpart to the Digital Public Library of America (DPLA), and the new version offers support for exhibits and educational resources about the state of Michigan and the people who live there. Many of our DPLA hubs are initiatives with close ties to state-based memory portals, and Michigan’s challenges and learnings offer useful insight for the whole DPLA Network.

The Michigan Service Hub was created in 2015 as a collaborative project by the Library of Michigan, Wayne State University, the University of Michigan, Michigan State University, Western Michigan University, and the Midwest Collaborative for Library Services. The service hub works with archives, libraries, museums, and historical societies around Michigan to help them share their publicly accessible, online collections more widely through the DPLA and Michigan Memories. Funding for the new site was provided in part by the Institute of Museum and Library Services through the Library of Michigan.

Speaker:
Richard C. Adler is the coordinator of the Michigan Service Hub, part of the hub network of the Digital Public Library of America (DPLA). He has traveled around the state to meet with staff at cultural institutions and work with them to share their online collections with the DPLA and the newly rebuilt Michigan Memories.

localized.title: DPLA Hub Spotlight: The New Michigan Memories
localized.description:
Join us as we spotlight the recent relaunch of Michigan Memories, a website that allows users to search the online collections of cultural institutions all around the state. Michigan Memories is the Michigan-centric counterpart to the Digital Public Library of America (DPLA), and the new version offers support for exhibits and educational resources about the state of Michigan and the people who live there. Many of our DPLA hubs are initiatives with close ties to state-based memory portals, and Michigan’s challenges and learnings offer useful insight for the whole DPLA Network.

The Michigan Service Hub was created in 2015 as a collaborative project by the Library of Michigan, Wayne State University, the University of Michigan, Michigan State University, Western Michigan University, and the Midwest Collaborative for Library Services. The service hub works with archives, libraries, museums, and historical societies around Michigan to help them share their publicly accessible, online collections more widely through the DPLA and Michigan Memories. Funding for the new site was provided in part by the Institute of Museum and Library Services through the Library of Michigan.

Speaker:
Richard C. Adler is the coordinator of the Michigan Service Hub, part of the hub network of the Digital Public Library of America (DPLA). He has traveled around the state to meet with staff at cultural institutions and work with them to share their online collections with the DPLA and the newly rebuilt Michigan Memories.

snippet.title: Creating Warwick - Making of Arcane Season 2
snippet.description:
From the Hound of Underground to the Beast of Zaun. Warwick isn’t just a beast, he’s a bond. The design went through a lot of exploration to find the right balance between raw power and traces of humanity, in true memory of Vander.

We focused on how his body would move, how the mechanics would feel heavy but still organic. Every part needed to show more than just force, it had to tell a bit of what’s left inside him.

#Fortiche #Fortichers #Warwick

snippet.title: When a legendary synth designer shows up in the comments | In Memory of Vladimir Kuzmin
snippet.description:
To commemorate the passing of Vladimir Kuzmin, the renown inventor of the Formanta Polivoks synthesizer, and to raise funds for his family, an independent group of musicians and instrument makers held a memorial event in Moscow. They asked me to contribute a video message about his legacy. Since Vladimir Kuzmin had previously commented on my videos, which was mind-blowing to me, I decided to tell that story. It is a bit embarrassing, since I got a few things wrong in my videos that he corrected me on. But at least I enjoyed my errors tremendously, and he did not seem to be mad about them.

snippet.title: Salad Mug - DYNAMO DREAM, Ep1
snippet.description:
Feels so good to finally post this! Unending thanks to all the friends who worked to help make this happen, and all of the folks over on the patreon! 

A lot changed over the course of making this episode (you can probably feel it), and while I'm really excited about this episode, I'm even more excited to keep everything moving for the next bit; the big goal is to be able to finish these things a bit faster than every 3 years :P 

Thanks so much for watching- I hope you enjoy it. 

If you DID enjoy it and want to chip in a bit financially for future episodes, I've documented a ton of the process (and shared a bunch of assets) over on my Patreon. Mostly VFX/blender tutorials and such, but also more general breakdowns, too, and I'd of course love to see you there. 
http://www.patreon.com/IanHubert

Also, HUGE thanks to Impossible Acoustic for being down to take on this project! The degree to which the audio sculpts the end experience here is absolutely wild. 
https://www.impossibleacoustic.com

Composited in After Effects, 
All 3d work in Blender (blender.org)

Huge thanks again, to everyone :D

snippet.description:
First Episode Here: https://youtu.be/LsGZ_2RuJ2A

Hoh man- the little compressed instagram version of this breakdown has been reposted so many times I figured it'd be good to release a version with a couple more pixels!

I've been really excited about this type of workflow in terms of what it means for making crazy films in a garage, and I've been experimenting a bunch with it in the months since (tons of viewport compositing in Blender. All the CG stuff in this video is blender's realtime eevee engine, which has just been a blast). I've been posting lots of breakdowns/tuts/experiments on the patreon (thank you to everyone over there!):
https://www.patreon.com/IanHubert
Although I'm still working on full-on- tutorials I'll be posting here for everyone pretty quick. Almost done! Bit off more than I could chew for a minute here :P

snippet.title: Finding Volo’s Voice | Fin Argus | Star Wars: Beyond Victory | Available on Meta Quest
snippet.description:
Go behind the scenes with Fin Argus, voice talent of Volo Bolus, a driven four-armed podracer from Star Wars: Beyond Victory. Learn more about using ILM’s magic mirror motion capture technology to see characters reflect their movements in real-time while working with the team at ILM. By tapping into a younger version of their own personality for the voice and navigating the precise physical requirements of a mocap suit, this lifelong Star Wars fan shares the joy of fulfilling a childhood dream.

Star Wars: Beyond Victory is available now on Meta Quest 3 and 3S.

snippet.title: Podracer Talk Radio | ILM
snippet.description:
Tune into this ambient radio broadcast straight from the world of Star Wars: Beyond Victory. From a station dedicated to speed on the planet Malastare, get a first look into the podracing subculture, featuring a series of interviews with local competitors, ranging from the optimistic racer Coy Vrizh and the entitled, wealthy Paghee’dhe to the ruthless twins Staka and Raka, who race under Jabba the Hutt's banner. Listeners are treated to colorful galactic advertisements—including a promotion for Seezelslak’s mobile cantina and a Nar Shaddaa tourism spot funded by Grakkus the Hutt. Between interviews with the racers, including Volo Bolus, the broadcast captures the high-stakes atmosphere of the circuit, where racing philosophies often lean toward sabotage and survival.

Star Wars: Beyond Victory is on sale now through May 5th on Meta Quest.

https://www.meta.com/experiences/star-wars-beyond-victory/9460903453969753/?srsltid=AfmBOopi4cvTIJLcZ5lsZ3GGpE_-8wYquzQE3wVgjK0_re8Q9T80jIRh

snippet.title: How Would I Edit Your Photo? with Scott Kelby | The Grid Ep 702
snippet.description:
In this episode of The Grid, Scott Kelby edits a collection of viewer-submitted photos, showing exactly how he'd approach each image from start to finish. He tackles everything from composition, white balance, and perspective correction to sharpening, masking, sky replacements, and AI-powered editing in Lightroom, Camera Raw, and Photoshop. Scott also shares practical advice on when to crop, when to fake shallow depth of field, why Adaptive Color has become one of his favorite tools, and the techniques he relies on to solve real-world editing challenges. Whether you shoot sports, landscapes, architecture, wildlife, or travel, you'll pick up plenty of editing tips you can put to work on your own photos.

ABOUT THE GRID PHOTOGRAPHY PODCAST
The Grid is a live talk show about photography, Photoshop, Lightroom, and other industry-related topics. Each week features a different guest (in-studio or online), and viewers are encouraged to chime in live here on YouTube, on KelbyOne.com, or on Scott Kelby's Facebook page: https://www.facebook.com/SKelby.

Visit: https://kelbyone.com/
 
ABOUT SCOTT KELBY
Scott Kelby is a renowned photographer, bestselling author, and educator, best known as the President and CEO of KelbyOne, an online educational community for photographers, Photoshop, and Lightroom users. He is a leading voice in photography training, having authored over 100 books, including the top-selling The Digital Photography Book.

ABOUT ERIK KUNA
Erik is the Vice President of Operations for KelbyOne and a passionate rocket launch photographer. His goal is to create images that help educate people about the space industry and inspire them to learn more about the beauty of space exploration. His passion was ignited in 2015 by seeing the SpaceX Falcon 9 booster land successfully. He felt like from that moment, he had to be part of documenting and capturing the beauty and inspiration of spaceflight, and he has never looked back.

snippet.title: One ON1 with Scott Kelby Ep. 18: Sky Swap AI, Snapshots & Versions
snippet.description: In this episode of One ON1, Scott Kelby shares several Sky Swap AI tips that can make your composites look more natural, including how to eliminate edge halos with the Fade Edge slider, refine tricky sky masks, add realistic reflections, and choose the right masking model for landscapes versus architecture. Then Dylan Kotecki joins Scott to explore Snapshots and Versions, showing how to create multiple creative looks from a single image, compare them side by side, and batch-export your favorites without duplicating files. If you've overlooked either of these features, this episode is packed with practical tips that can easily become part of your everyday editing workflow.

snippet.description:
You don't need a crew to shoot portraits like a pro. Gilmar Smith shows you how to plan, pack, light, shoot, and deliver professional portrait sessions entirely on your own. Learn the pre-production questions that protect your time and your paycheck, the packing and gear systems that let one person do the work of a full team, and the on-set strategies she used to photograph 50 realtors in two days — solo. snippet.title: Why Your Drums Feel Dead
snippet.description:
*Subjective opinions within, those who do not understand subjective opinion may be excused lol*

*100% music in this video composed/produced by me.

SUPPORT MUSIC AND BUY MY ALBUMS! https://noiretblancvie.bandcamp.com/

In keeping with the theme of "hey, why not go make some music", I realized, I have a lot of drum machines, and I kinda only used them sparingly. Mainly because it's soooooo much easier to just use plugins, but once again in the theme of "easy doesn't mean better" convenience isn't the thing that pushes us to create, well at least me.  A box, especially a rhythm box has this almost primal tactile vibe. The drum machine isn't the most useful when you could just pull up a loop in your DAW, but the Dave Smith Instruments Tempest being the #1 instrument I use just for fun.  (Out side of a literal piano) has always brought me back to the feeling of "why do we love rhythm instruments".  While I've got the Elektron Analog RYTM, the Drumbrute yadda yadda, the "tool" remains the tool. The groove is within us, we must extract it and with the help of the tool, not the other way around.

snippet.title: You're Not Creating, You're Assembling.
snippet.description:
*Subjective opinions within, those who do not understand subjective opinion may be excused lol*

*100% music in this video composed/produced by me.

SUPPORT MUSIC AND BUY MY ALBUMS! https://noiretblancvie.bandcamp.com/

Often When I'm talking to someone from the channel they're speaking to me about how they're not really getting traction in their creative process.  They're saying "I keep buying gear, I like gear, but I really want to finish more songs" They ask "How do you finish songs, would something like X or Y piece be more conducive to finishing tracks", my answer has always remained the same for many years.  What does your actual life look like, maybe you're not finishing songs, because you don't feel in your life there's something worth writing about? That's not an attack, that's my honest answer, I've always felt compelled to do music when there's a reason.  I almost can't.  No synth, Dave Smith Tempest, Moog Sub 37 name that thing has compelled me to create more than just living life. Stevie Wonder made an album called "Songs in the Key of Life" what a perfect way to phase what I'm trying to say to you in this video.

So yeah, I thought that I'd make ANOTHER video about the Dave Smith Tempest which sorta has nothing to do with the Tempest at all HAHAHA.  I imagine if you're actually still watching my channel after all this time you get it at this point.  I've never really been the "gear" guy, I've been the "what do you really want outta this journey" guy. snippet.title: You Only Think Vintage Synths Sound Better
snippet.description:
*Subjective opinions within, those who do not understand subjective opinion may be excused lol*

*100% music in this video composed/produced by me.

SUPPORT MUSIC AND BUY MY ALBUMS! https://noiretblancvie.bandcamp.com/

So I was playing my Waldorfs, just making some music and looking for inspiration, and a thought came to me... Am I only using my Waldorf XT because I "like it" not because it's actually better in anyway?  While there are so many videos comparing synths online, I keep wondering....WHY? Like, what's the actual goal with this.  I personally wonder if there's psychology behind why some can't just move forward and make sound instead of thinking "I wonder if X makes sounds like Y" when the shortest answer would easily be "why not just get the X?".  When I think about music I'm often confused by the idea of all this... so maybe ask yourself this.... "What's your goal".  When you see life as only one constant stream, you cannot go back, only forward, I think so many of the choices I make to create come from that.  Rather than compare, rather than spend my time purchasing, why not be content, why not just create....?  A question for you today.

snippet.title: Bridging intelligence: practical library applications of AI and linked data at OCLC
snippet.description:
Due to popular demand from those unable to attend the IFLA WLIC Conference in Astana, Kazakhstan in 2025, we ran an updated version of session, Building Intelligence: Practical library applications of AI and Linked Data at OCLC.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the way we access, share, and interpret information, but its potential is only as strong as the data that powers it. In this session, TJ Godsey explores our practical applications of AI in resource sharing, offering real-life examples that demonstrate its transformative impact. While, Axel Kaschte also provides an update on our ongoing work with linked data, highlighting how it enhances discoverability and interoperability. Most importantly, they connect the dots between AI and linked data, underscoring how the structured, interconnected nature of linked data can strengthen the accuracy and relevance of artificial intelligence in ways that help advance librarianship. Join us to discover how these technologies are working together to redefine how libraries can serve their communities.

Download the FAQ PDF for this topic: https://oc.lc/practical-ai-applications

To learn more about Linked data: https://www.oclc.org/en/linked-data.html

To learn more about Meridian: https://www.oclc.org/en/meridian.html

Kwesi Christian helps empower OCLC’s teams by providing them with the latest hardware and software tools and resources they need to deliver on their promise to libraries. He talked with us about the importance of his role, as well as how libraries supported him during his childhood and continue to create lasting impacts in his life (and the lives of others) today.

Want to be part of OCLC’s technology with a purpose? Learn about the impacts we make, our company culture, and available career opportunities at http://oc.lc/careers.

snippet.title: Introducing the "Library Collaboration as a Strategic Choice" OCLC Research report
snippet.description:
In this short video, Brian Lavoie, Senior Research Scientist, introduces the OCLC Research report he authored, "Library Collaboration as a Strategic Choice: Evaluating Options for Acquiring Capacity."

This report explores library collaboration as a key strategy for academic libraries in acquiring needed capacity, but also contextualizes it as one sourcing approach among a range of options available to libraries. You'll come away with insights and resources that can help your academic library think about whether and how to choose collaborative options that meet your strategic goals.
 
➡️ Download and read the full report here: http://oc.lc/strategic-collaboration

snippet.title: Office Hours | Saturday | August 01, 2026
snippet.description:
Office Hours | Saturday | August 01, 2026
We are here every day to answer your questions about media and production!

Submit your questions anytime https://www.askofficehours.global
Join our global community https://officehours.global

00:00:00 Intro
00:00:32 Is this NSH Electric Telescopic crane worth $13,000? [link] and [link]
00:10:23 In a modern broadcast camera, other than supply power, what can a CCU do that a RCP cannot do as isn’t most color processing is done at the camera?
00:19:56 An interesting BTS on "Adolescence" on Netflix. Is it really a One Take production? What other films use this technique?[link]
00:27:35 How many people are using the Elgato Network Adaptor with their StreamDecks, and what is your use case?

00:58:57 Aside from on Office Hours, do you have a mic/audio meter always visible, and where in your audio chain are you monitoring?

snippet.title: The Rundown (Episode 92)
snippet.description:
Language is the operating system of our world—turning storytellers into civilizations. From writing and the printing press to smartphones and AI, every new technology has upgraded how we communicate while introducing new bugs. Now machines don’t just carry our words; they generate them. As language keeps changing, how will it change us?

Technology is not just transforming the world—it’s redefining what it means to live, connect, and create in the digital age. The rapid acceleration of technological change presents both profound challenges and new opportunities, fundamentally altering how we relate to each other and understand ourselves.

On The Rundown Show, we dive deep into the forces reshaping our world, exploring not just the 'what' but the 'why' behind the latest trends. Each week, we offer a thoughtful, philosophical lens on how technology is influencing human connection, society, and the ways we experience life itself. Join us as we unpack and critically examine the technologies shaping our future, helping you navigate this evolving landscape with deeper insight and understanding.

snippet.title: Can a 3D artist actually leave Windows?
snippet.description:
After 6 months of using Kubuntu 25.10 as my daily operating system, I have many thoughts on the differences between using Windows and Linux! And as a 3D artist, sound designer and video editor, I have wanted to make this transition for a while, and I'm finally starting to see how I will be able to make the switch. Also, I have to admit, there are probably some unusual comparisons in this video, but I've tried to include everything that's important for me in an OS I wish to use every day!

0:00 Intro
0:39 What I like about Windows
3:34 What I don't like about Windows
8:35 What I like about Kubuntu
12:49 What I don't like about Kubuntu
16:39 Why I still dual boot
17:48 My plan to leave Windows

snippet.title: Experimenting with Opencode on Linux (as a longtime Windows user)
snippet.description:
In this video I'll be demonstrating how I've been using Large Langauge Models (LLMs) to interact with my computer using just natural language. I'm using Opencode to connect with different LLM models, and I'm giving them full access to my new installation of Kubuntu 25.10.

⚠️ Warning: The agentic AI setup in this video has full read/write access to my computer with no sandboxing or safety restrictions. This can go very wrong, very quickly. Only attempt something like this if you understand the risks and are willing to accept full responsibility for what happens.

My Kubuntu 25.10 tutorial:
https://youtu.be/Pe8uUMxPyTc

Learn more about opencode here:
https://opencode.ai

Feel free to support me on Patreon if you want the animated & looping Layers and Lights wallpaper (4k 60fps): https://www.patreon.com/posts/85188752?collection=241756

00:00 Intro
00:49 Why open source?
02:16 Why Kubuntu?
03:14 How to install Kubuntu in 3 steps
03:51 What is opencode?
05:09 How to install Opencode
06:21 Checking my Blender installation
07:23 Organizing my downloads folder
08:44 The purpose of Opencode
10:18 Using 3 agents simultaneously
13:43 Setting an animated desktop wallpaper
14:49 How I've been using AI agents on Linux so far
18:40 Pros and cons for AI agents
19:42 The future of Kubuntu

snippet.title: Learn how to animate and render a fish in Blender! (Beginner friendly)
snippet.description:
Hello! Today I'm testing out a new format on my channel: A MEGA TUTORIAL 📖🧠 It covers absolutely every single step from start to finish! We will animate a fish in Blender - no matter how long it takes. This means that this video is my most in-depth youtube tutorial yet, where we will be animating a fish (as seen in my previous video https://youtu.be/7TZaAAifdy0)

Project file here (free): https://www.patreon.com/posts/151715503/

This tutorial is very beginner friendly, because I try to make no assumptions about your previous knowledge, and I try my absolute best to explain every single step, and why we are doing what we are doing. This means that this video shows the entire process completely raw and unedited. It includes all my mistakes and every reasoning I make during the process, and I hope it's valuable for you!

I am testing out this longer format, so if you think this 'mega tutorial' concept is an interesting format, please let me know if there's any topic or technique you would like to see me go in-depth with like this! Thanks for watching!

00:00:00 What we'll be creating
00:01:19 Finding a fish model
00:16:10 Curve path setup
00:38:15 Animation part 1
01:05:06 Model optimizaitons
01:22:35 Animation part 2
01:43:09 Shape keys
02:02:13 Texturing & lighting
02:34:17 Camera movement
02:58:15 Motion blur R&D
03:21:19 Final result

snippet.title: The secret to easy fish animation in Blender!
snippet.description:
Hello! I've experimented with fish animations for a few weeks now, and the result is this fish locomotion workflow I didn't even know I needed!

💾 Get the free tutorial project file here: https://www.patreon.com/posts/151545504/
⭐ Get the Experimental Shark Curve Rig: https://www.patreon.com/posts/151555947/
⭐ Get the Looping fish chasing bait scene: https://www.patreon.com/posts/151554285/

Assets used:
Burst-and-coast reference video: https://youtu.be/y9lUWd5NGms
PolyHaven sand texture (CC0): https://polyhaven.com/a/aerial_beach_01

Fish models by ffish.asia on Sketchfab (CC0):
Pennant coralfish: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/cc0-pennant-coralfish-h-acuminatus-27f435f82a0443ef8980b42e4bd9105e
Pale Bleak, Z. platypus: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/cc0-pale-bleak-z-platypus-animation-83a46c7261ef471194f0a268c5b5aafc
Smooth Hammerhead Shark: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/cc0-smooth-hammerhead-shark-3d1e1898e87c4187bbf3e6a264a9f933

Software used:
Blender version 5.0: https://www.blender.org/download/releases/5-0/

Affiliate links:
🚗 Bonus car model shown at the end of the video is made using Polygoniq's Traffiq asset pack: https://www.superhivemarket.com/products/car-library-traffiq-vehicles-for-blender?ref=1129 and the Botaniq asset pack: https://www.superhivemarket.com/products/botaniq-trees?ref=1129

🎵 Music used in this video: https://share.epidemicsound.com/m6whxf

snippet.description:
TL;DR: This tutorial introduces the AccuFACE 2 facial mocap system for iClone 8, designed to boost real-time facial tracking accuracy and stability for Character Creator 5 (CC5) HD characters. Learn how to achieve high-fidelity facial animation from subtle lip movements to dynamic performances, solving common mocap challenges for 3D artists and studios.

- Leverage GPU acceleration and a newly trained AI model in AccuFACE 2 to achieve real-time, full-frame facial tracking, specifically optimized for Character Creator 5 (CC5) HD characters, delivering significantly improved accuracy and stability.
- Ensure robust facial motion capture with AccuFACE 2's blur-resilient tracking, capable of capturing faces as small as 120x120 pixels while maintaining fidelity, even during large head turns and fast motion blur.
- Enhance tracking universality through AccuFACE 2's advanced model, optimized for diverse ethnicities and skin tones, automatically applying gamma correction to normalize facial lighting and reduce tracking drift.
- Integrate AccuFACE 2 seamlessly with iClone 8 and Motion LIVE, utilizing the new Curve System and AccuLIPS for phoneme-based tongue animation to achieve highly precise mouth shapes, subtle micro-movements, and realistic speech.
- Refine performances using the Grab Neutral Pose function to redefine facial baselines and utilize the all-new Motion LIVE Curve System with hundreds of CC5 HD facial morph sliders for granular control over animation style and expression.

❓ Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: How does AccuFACE 2 improve facial tracking accuracy?
A: AccuFACE 2 significantly improves accuracy and stability through GPU acceleration and a newly trained AI tracking model with specialized mouth-tracking optimizations, tailored for CC5 HD characters.

Q: Can AccuFACE 2 track faces under challenging conditions?
A: Yes, AccuFACE 2 features long-distance, blur-resilient tracking, successfully capturing faces as small as 120x120 pixels and maintaining stability even with large head turns or fast motion blur.

Q: How does AccuFACE 2 integrate with iClone 8 for full animation control?
A: AccuFACE 2 tightly integrates with iClone 8 and Motion LIVE, allowing real-time streaming of facial data, and enables further refinement using the advanced Curve System and combination with AccuLIPS for realistic speech.

- Customize morph curves and utilize nonlinear tweening for professionally refined facial animation.
- Drive multiple character morphs with a single tracking marker for richer, expressive performances.
- Ensure stable tracking performance through extreme head rotations, diverse skin tones, and challenging lighting conditions.

❓ Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: Why is AccuFACE 2 the best facial mocap for CC5 HD characters? 
A: Its new AI model communicates directly with CC5's native HD Expression Profile, driving 262 blendshapes and 128 corrective morphs in real time to capture intricate facial nuances and mouth details with surgical precision. 

Q: How can I customize facial mocap with Expression Curves? 
A: You can fine-tune motion timing and intensity to add exaggeration or follow-through. It lets you push subtle performance into stylized, highly expressive cartoon animation 

Q: What video sources can be used with AccuFACE 2?
A: Track live via webcams or laptop cameras, or import pre-recorded clips (MP4, MOV, AVI) from phones, head-rigs, or online. Installing the K-Lite Codec Pack ensures seamless playback for virtually any video format.

- Integrate iClone 8 animation workflows with 3D Guided Generation and 3D to Video to stylize output and add dynamic voice performances with consistent motion.
- Control specific emotional parameters (Emotion, Tone, Speaking Speed, Voice Style) directly within the Speech Text field for precise voice delivery.
- Manage complex dialogues for up to two characters using Multiple Talking Avatars, allowing for custom voice assignments and natural pacing with delay times.

A: Use AI Studio's Talking Avatar feature to create high-quality voices at a lower credit cost compared to other methods like Seedance.

Q: Can I create dialogues for multiple talking avatars simultaneously?
A: Yes, AI Studio's Multiple Talking Avatars feature supports up to two characters, allowing you to build full conversations with independent voice assignments and customizable pauses.

snippet.title: NIMROD
snippet.description:
In a distant future, where a power struggle between the ruling council and the dissidents who stand against it lasts a millennia, a hunter tracks down the last of the remaining dissidents and brings them to justice. 
Nimrod is a sci-fi proof of concept film, it exists purely because it was fun to make.

Written and Directed by - Sava Živković
Produced at Bauk Pictures
Produced by - Slobodan Danilović and Sava Živković
Characters Designed and Created by - Antonio Esparza
Character Rigging - Lucas Salamon
Animation Lead - Slobodan Danilović 
Animators - Goran Ugarčina and Branko Jeremić
Unreal Engine Crowd TD - Ryan Daly
Voice Performance - Andrew Howell aka Deadpedal
Music and Sound Design - Adis Kutkut Billain

Support the work and learn on Patreon -  https://www.patreon.com/c/SavaZivkovic

snippet.title: In Our Wake | Process on Patreon
snippet.description:
The process for In Our Wake was documented in its entirety and broken up into 4 videos, with total runtime of 5 hours. A combination of sped up footage with real time commentary, documenting the entire creation process from initial ideation, previz, editing, environments, lighting, character asset, animation, fx and final polishing. This is not a step by step tutorial, but a comprehensive insight into my methodology and thinking process of how I go about producing something like this and can be applied to bigger projects.


All 4 parts are live on Patreon - https://www.patreon.com/c/SavaZivkovic

snippet.title: Destiny 2: The Final Shape | SCREEB QUEEN
snippet.description:
Over the course of last year I’ve had an absolute privilege and a pleasure to revisit the world of Destiny 2 and direct 4 more cinematics for the conclusion of the epic space opera, The Final Shape.

Working with a team of incredibly talented and passionate people at Axis Studios, we’ve tackled stories ranging from abstract and metaphor infused premonitions, to dream sequences, to pure nightmare fuel, all the way to high octane bug squashing action set pieces.

My heartfelt thank you goes out to the entire Final Shape team at Axis and to the team at Bungie for entrusting me with these unique stories.

Directed by Sava Zivkovic
Executive Producer – Laura Yeo
Producer – Natasha Shetye
Art Director – Emrys Ryan
CGI supervisor – John Huikku

Produced at Axis Studios 2023-2024

snippet.title: NexLink Wireless Pairing
snippet.description:
NexLink is Sound Devices' proprietary long-distance protocol for remote-controlling wireless transmitters. By pairing transmitters to an Astral receiver, you are able to change all settings from the receiver without touching the transmitter itself. Now, this initial pairing sequence can also be performed wirelessly!

To learn more about NexLink, visit this article: https://www.sounddevices.com/nexlink-explained/

To learn about the A20-HH mic visit: https://www.sounddevices.com/product/a20-hh/

snippet.title: How to Create Stylized Feathers and Fur in Blender
snippet.description:

🛠️ MoGraph Toolbox (Free Tools)

❤️ Support the Channel

Patreon

Skillshare

────────────────────────────────────────

🎨 Tag me in your artwork!

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/southernshotty/
X (Twitter): https://twitter.com/SouthernShotty

@SouthernShotty

────────────────────────────────────────

Want soft, stylized fur or feather systems without millions of polygons? In this tutorial, I'll show you how to build a lightweight Geometry Nodes feather system that looks smooth, performs well in Eevee, and avoids the harsh shadows and artifacts common with traditional scattering methods. We'll also add subtle animation, randomized colors, and a custom shader to bring everything to life.

This workflow is perfect for stylized characters, creatures, cozy scenes, and game-ready assets where you need a clean look without sacrificing performance.

In This Video You'll Learn

• Creating a procedural feather system with Geometry Nodes
• Setting up Blender's Scatter on Surface modifier
• Smoothing feather shading with custom normals
• Adding subtle procedural feather animation
• Randomizing feather colors using named attributes
• Building a stylized feather shader from scratch
• Creating gradients and feather texture details
• Adding artificial rim lighting for stylized renders
• Eevee settings for cleaner fur and feather rendering
• Layering multiple feather systems for richer results
• Using weight painting to control feather placement

Traditional fur and feather systems often require extremely high densities to hide visible intersections and harsh shading. This workflow instead smooths the lighting using custom normals while keeping the geometry lightweight, resulting in cleaner renders and much better viewport performance.

Tools Used

• Blender Geometry Nodes
• Scatter on Surface Modifier
• Eevee
• Noise Textures
• Custom Normal Workflow
• Procedural Materials

If this tutorial helped you, leave a like and let me know what stylized Geometry Nodes tutorial you'd like to see next.

Subscribe for more Blender tutorials, Geometry Nodes workflows, stylized rendering techniques, and practical production tips.

00:00 – Overview
00:27 – Building the System
03:37 – Geometry Nodes Setup
07:18 – Adding Animation
10:20 – Creating the Shader
17:00 – Final Tweaks

Transparent Materials Finally Work in Blender 5.2

Blender 5.2 introduces a surprisingly powerful new feature to the Principled BSDF shader: Thin Wall. While it sounds simple, this option solves several long-standing transparency problems and makes materials like paper, leaves, frosted glass, bubbles, and thin translucent surfaces both easier to create and faster to render.

In this video, we'll explore how Thin Wall works, compare it to older Blender workflows, and build a creepy frosted-glass effect that takes advantage of the new system.

In This Video You'll Learn

• What the new Thin Wall option does
• Why transparent planes were problematic before
• Replacing Solidify modifiers for thin transparent materials
• Creating bubble and thin-film effects
• Better foliage and leaf rendering
• Fixing Blender's dark window glass problem
• Faster transparent material rendering
• Creating frosted glass materials
• Building a horror-style silhouette effect behind glass
• Using noise and grunge maps to create realistic surface imperfections

Features Covered

• Thin Wall in Principled BSDF
• Transmission Materials
• Subsurface Scattering
• Bubble Materials
• Foliage Shading
• Glass Windows
• Frosted Glass
• Roughness Workflows
• Bump Mapping
• Lighting Through Transparent Surfaces

Why This Matters

Thin Wall isn't just a quality-of-life feature.

It improves realism, reduces setup complexity, eliminates the need for many Solidify modifiers, fixes several transparency edge cases, and can even improve render performance in scenes with foliage, paper, glass, and other thin materials.

For environment artists, product visualizers, stylized artists, and VFX creators, this is one of the most useful rendering improvements coming to Blender 5.2.

What material are you most excited to use Thin Wall on?

Blender 5.2's NEW Cloth Simulator is Crazy

Blender 5.2 introduces a brand-new experimental cloth simulation system built directly into Geometry Nodes, giving artists unprecedented control over cloth behavior, collisions, forces, and even tearing effects. In this video, we'll explore every major setting, explain what the new nodes do, and build a reusable peeling effect that can be applied to almost any object.

Unlike Blender's traditional cloth system, this new workflow feels much closer to procedural simulation tools found in high-end VFX software, while still being accessible directly inside Blender.

In This Video You'll Learn

• How to enable the experimental cloth simulator in Blender 5.2
• Understanding Stretchiness vs Bending Stiffness
• Pin groups and cloth constraints
• Simulation quality settings and solver controls
• Mass, friction, damping, and collision settings
• The new cloth tearing system
• Voronoi-based tearing patterns
• Custom force fields inside Geometry Nodes
• Geometry-based collisions and collider collections
• Creating procedural wind effects
• Building a reusable peeling-away effect
• Baking Geometry Nodes simulations for faster playback

Features Covered

• Cloth Dynamics Node
• Geometry Collider Node
• Custom Force Node
• Tearing Thresholds
• Voronoi Tear Patterns
• Simulation Zones
• Procedural Wind Systems
• Collection-Based Collisions
• Bake Node Workflow

Why This Update Matters

This is one of the biggest simulation upgrades Blender has received in years.

Because everything happens inside Geometry Nodes, you're no longer limited to traditional cloth modifiers and force objects. You can build custom simulation systems, procedural effects, advanced collisions, and reusable setups that would have previously required significantly more complex workflows.

For technical artists, motion designers, VFX artists, and procedural workflow enthusiasts, this opens up a huge number of possibilities.

What if Blender could become a full pixel art workflow tool with live previews, pixel-perfect cameras, outlines, dithering, toon shading, and even image-to-pixel conversion… all inside Eevee?

In this video, I’m showing off Pixel Blender Kit — a free Blender addon designed to make creating real-time pixel art dramatically easier.

ouTube Description

Advice for Becoming a 3D Artist in 2026 — From a Blender Professional

There’s been a growing fear online that there’s “no future” for Blender artists anymore. As someone who’s worked professionally in the industry for over 10 years — including projects connected to some of the largest companies in the world — I wanted to make a grounded, honest video about what I think actually matters if you want to build a career as a 3D artist in 2026.

This is not another doom-posting AI video.

Instead, these are five practical lessons from my own experience working professionally in Blender, motion design, and creative production.

In This Video You'll Learn

• Why understanding art fundamentals matters more than ever
• How composition, lighting, color theory, and visual strategy separate artists from tools
• Why workflow speed and non-destructive processes are becoming critical professional skills
• How to identify “safe skills” that are harder to automate
• Why niche specialization matters in modern creative careers
• The communication skills that help artists grow faster than technically stronger peers
• How to handle client feedback professionally and reduce endless revisions
• Why adaptability matters more than fear

Topics Covered

• Art theory and visual communication
• Creative direction and brand strategy
• Workflow optimization
• Specialized career paths
• Technical vs creative skills
• Client communication
• Feedback systems
• Career growth in changing industries

Resources Mentioned

• The Five C’s of Cinematography
• Painting With Light
• Adobe Color
• Studio case studies from companies like Giant Ant

Sponsor

Thanks to Storyblocks for sponsoring this video.
Their library includes human-made footage, textures, templates, music, sound effects, and practical assets that help speed up creative workflows.

Why I Made This Video

I know a lot of newer artists are discouraged right now. But I genuinely still believe there is a future for Blender artists and traditional creative work.

The industry is changing — but that doesn’t mean creativity is disappearing.

Call to Action

If this video helped or encouraged you, let me know in the comments.

Also feel free to share your own advice for newer artists entering the industry.

Subscribe for more Blender tutorials, professional workflow advice, animation, stylized art, and creative industry discussions.

snippet.title: From Ansel Adams to Steve Jobs: The Evolution of Photography's Hall of Fame
snippet.description:
Mark Braun, Chairman of the Board at the International Photography Hall of Fame (IPHF), joins Frederick Van Johnson for an enlightening conversation about honoring photography's greatest contributors, the organization's evolution from physical museum to global digital platform, and why understanding photographic history matters in today's rapidly changing landscape.

TOPICS COVERED:

The mission of IPHF and who qualifies for induction (00:00)
Mark's journey from corporate America to leading IPHF (10:10)
Why Steve Jobs was inducted into the Photography Hall of Fame (10:14)
The nomination and voting process explained (10:43)
Transitioning from physical museum to virtual organization (10:35)
The importance of studying the masters—from composition to darkroom techniques (10:30)
How technology is reshaping photography and the Hall of Fame's role (10:48)
Upcoming Indianapolis awards ceremony and events (11:00)

FEATURED INDUCTEES MENTIONED:

Ansel Adams, Steve McCurry, Joseph Karsh, Steve Jobs, Graham Nash, John and Tom Knoll (Photoshop creators), and many more

UPCOMING EVENTS:

Indianapolis Awards Weekend - October 11-12, 2025

FREE Lecture by Jeff Shewe on digital photography (Saturday, Oct 12)
Awards ceremony honoring 2025 inductees
4-day photography book workshop with Karen Pasalas
Panel discussion moderated by Frederick Van Johnson

RESOURCES:

Website: iphf.org
Email: info@iphf.org
Opportunities: Memberships, volunteering, board positions, photo competitions, nominations
Whether you're shooting with an iPhone or medium format film, this conversation offers valuable insights into photography's rich history and exciting future.

ABOUT THE GUEST:

Mark Braun is the Chairman of the Board at the International Photography Hall of Fame, bringing his corporate leadership experience and lifelong passion for photography to guide the organization through its 60th year and digital transformation.

ABOUT THE HOST:

Frederick Van Johnson is a photographer, educator, and Secretary of the IPHF Board of Directors, as well as Chairman of the International Advisory Council.

#Photography #IPHF #PhotographyHistory #ThisWeekInPhoto #PhotographyPodcast

snippet.title: Generative AI and the Evolution of Art - with Colin Smith
snippet.description:
In this episode of This Week in Photo, host Frederick Van Johnson is joined by Colin Smith, founder of Photoshop Cafe, to explore the capabilities of Photoshop's new generative AI. They dive into the application's transformative features, how they reshape creative workflows, the potential and limitations of the technology, and its impact on the future of digital art and photography. Colin provides an in-depth look at practical use cases and demonstrates the tool's ability to generate and manipulate images in unprecedented ways. This episode offers a comprehensive understanding of how generative AI is set to revolutionize the industry.

snippet.title: The Power of Personal Projects: Keron Psillas on Passion, Photography & Purpose
snippet.description:
Join Frederick as he sits down with acclaimed photographer and author Keron Psillas for an inspiring conversation about the power of personal projects in creative development. Keron shares her journey from publishing to photography, the emotional depth behind her long-term project on genocide, and the importance of pursuing work that is deeply meaningful. Discover how passion, dedication, and collaboration can transform not only your art but your life. Whether you’re an artist, photographer, or creative of any kind, this episode will motivate you to dive deeper into your own projects and embrace the infinite pursuit of creativity.

📚 Learn more about her books and exhibitions
💬 Leave your thoughts and questions in the comments!

snippet.title: Spotlighting Black Women Photographers | BWP × Flickr Grant Celebration
snippet.description:
On May 8th, I was joined by Genesis Falls for a powerful livestream featuring the work and impact of Black Women Photographers (BWP) — a global community founded by Polly Irungu, championing over 2,100 Black and African women creatives. 

https://blackwomenphotographers.com

Since 2020, BWP has been breaking barriers, offering grants, education, and exposure to photographers who deserve the spotlight.

Big thanks to our partners at SmugMug and Flickr, who share a passion for elevating creativity and storytelling across the globe!

✨ What’s on deck:

- The story behind this year's theme: The Spaces We Occupy
- Behind-the-scenes look at the judging process and grant prizes
- Featuring 10 standout runner-up photos
- Announcing the $5,000 grant winner LIVE! 🎉

You’ll meet amazing photographers, get inspired, and find out how to follow and support their work beyond today’s broadcast.

👉 Hit that Follow button and join us on Flickr, SmugMug, and TWiP for more inspiring events like this!

snippet.title: Matthew Jordan Smith: The Power of Personal Projects, Persistence, and Print
snippet.description:
In this episode, I sit down with my good friend Matthew Jordan Smith — celebrity photographer, author of Aretha Cool, and master storyteller — to dive into the powerful connection between personal projects, photography's future, and staying true to your vision in an AI-driven world.

You will discover:

- How Matthew turned a promise to Aretha Franklin into a celebrated book
- The impact of AI on the authenticity of photography
- Why printed photos and physical books matter more than ever
- How to stay creatively inspired, even without a big city around you
- Advice for photographers balancing art, career, and personal fulfillment

This conversation is a masterclass on passion, perseverance, and finding your voice as a creative. Drop your thoughts in the comments — and if you enjoyed it, don't forget to subscribe, like, and share with a friend! 

You can learn more about Matthew at thisweekinphoto.com.

snippet.title: Cha Che Chi Day Two
snippet.description:
Chabón, chango, chava, chela, checar, chicha, chichón, chido, chimichurri, chulo, churro —the ch* sounds reverberate throughout Latin America. And now, we bring all that rhythmic cacophony to you in typographic resonance—a virtual conference featuring Latin American typographic excellence and insight.

The Cha Che Chi conference was held online on March 3rd and 4th, as a two-day showcase of presentations and panels on what’s happening in Latin American typography today.

DAY TWO SCHEDULE
- Introduction / Ksenya Samarskaya
- #NiUnaMenos: The Collective Power of Women / Sol Matas, Yani Arabena, Cyla Costa, Fernanda Cozzi
- Why do we want new fonts? / Raphaël Verona
- Murals: Take the risk and go big / Ximena Jiménez
- Call to Action, Type in Political and Social contexts / Tulio Cerquize, Laureano Menéndez, Gustavo Greco, Daniel Sabino
- Type Tour: Pichação in São Paulo / Tony de Marco
- Imperfect letters from the south / Guillermo Vizzari
- Design in Translation / Beatriz Lozano
