snippet.title: Not Typecast: Two Women and their Typography at Mid-Century
snippet.description:
Briar Levit and Anne Galperin tell the stories of Ellen Raskin and Betti Broadwater Haft, two New York-based contemporaries: one an illustrator turned book designer, turned author and the other, a multidisciplinary designer who was one of the rare women to design a typeface for Photo-lettering Inc. These are just two of the many histories featured in the forthcoming book of essays, “Baseline Shift: Untold Stories of Women in Graphic Design History.”

- - - - 

About the Speakers

BRIAR LEVIT is an Associate Professor of Graphic Design at Portland State University. She studied at San Francisco State University for her undergraduate degree in graphic design and at Central Saint Martins in London for her MA in Communication Design. Levit spent her early career in publishing as Art Director of Bitch: Feminist Response to Pop Culture magazine as well as an independent book designer. Her self-initiated publications are walking books that challenge the existing hiking guide genre. More recently, Levit’s feature-length documentary, Graphic Means: A History of Graphic Design Production (2017) which follows design production from manual to digital methods, established an obsession with design history—particularly aspects not in the canon. She currently co-directs The People’s Graphic Design Archive with Louise Sandhaus and Brockett Horne and has edited a book of essays debuting October 26th, 2021 entitled “Baseline Shift: Previously Untold Stories of Women Throughout Graphic Design History.”

ANNE GALPERIN is an Associate Professor of Art, and Graphic Design program director at the State University of New York at New Paltz. She earned a BSc in Human Development and Social Policy from Northwestern University, and an MFA in 2D Design from Cranbrook Academy of Art. Before entering academia, Galperin edited and wrote for the Macmillan Publishing Company, was a freelance writer and researcher, and designed books in-house at Chronicle Books. Her body of work includes book design for alt-press, museum, and art book clients, including Four Walls Eight Windows/OR Books, the Walker Art Center, and Distributed Art Publishers. Her essay about American Designer Betti Broadwater Haft is included in “Baseline Shift: Untold Stories of Women in Graphic Design History”, edited by Briar Levit and to be released in late October 2021

snippet.title: Towards a Global Definition of Excellence in Type Design - Part 3: Arabic
snippet.description:
Meet some of the 25TDC Typeface Design Jury moderated by Nadine Chahine, Committee Co-Chair.

This is part 3 of a three part series. 

This year marks the expansion of TDC’s Typeface Design Competition with 3 extra categories added for Arabic, Indic, and CJK (Chinese, Japanese, and Korean) scripts. While TDC has long accepted entries in these categories, 2021 marks the first year with multiple dedicated judges for these categories. Each of these categories has 3 judges known for their expertise in that field.

In this video our inaugural judges discuss how one can define excellence in type design in each of these 3 categories, if there is anything there that is unique to that script’s historical printing and typographic history, and to discuss the general state of type design at this point in time.

If you are interested in submitting an original typeface design please visit: 
https://tdc.oneclub.org

snippet.title: “Person Place Thing” with Bobby Martin Jr.
snippet.description:
Virtual Event 
09.20.2021

Bobby C. Martin Jr. is co-founder of Champions Design, a branding and design agency headquartered in New York City.

He sets the relentless standard of design and vision for the agency he founded, with Jennifer Kinon, in 2010. Together they have partnered with a wide range of clients such as Amazon, Apple, Dartmouth College, Girl Scouts, MTV, the National Basketball Association and The Studio Museum in Harlem.

Martin recently illustrated his first children’s book “Have I Ever Told You Black Lives Matter” (Tilbury House). In 2020, he was featured in the renowned design publication, Eye Magazine’s iconic 100th issue.

He has lectured about brand identity around the world, sat on numerous awards juries, and has been a special guest on Design Matters, Design Observer and NPR’s Studio 360. Martin served as a board member of AIGA/NY from 2006-08, and the board of the Type Directors Club from 2014-2021. In 2019, Champions Design was named one of the 30 Most Important Companies in Design by Fast Company. Bobby Martin has won numerous international awards from the AIGA, Art Directors Club, Communication Arts, D&AD, and the TDC, among others. He is a graduate of Virginia Commonwealth University, and earned an MFA from the School of Visual Arts where he currently serves on the faculty.

Randy Cohen’s first professional work was writing humor pieces, essays, and stories for newspapers and magazines (The New Yorker, Harpers, the Atlantic, Young Love Comics). His first television work was writing for “Late Night With David Letterman” for which he won three Emmy awards. His fourth Emmy was for his work on Michael Moore’s “TV Nation.” He received a fifth Emmy as a result of a clerical error, and he kept it. For twelve years he wrote “The Ethicist,” a weekly column for the New York Times Magazine. In 2010, his first play, “The Punishing Blow,” ran at New York’s Clurman Theater. His most recent book, “Be Good: how to navigate the ethics of everything,” was published by Chronicle. He is currently the creator and host of Person Place Thing, a public radio program.

snippet.title: The Unity Studio templates | Build a design review application
snippet.description:
Learn how to build an interactive 3D building showcase in Unity Studio by repurposing a ready-made template, without C#.

Unity Studio is a web-based editor that helps teams create, collaborate on, and share interactive 3D experiences — without coding complexity. It's built for industries like manufacturing, automotive, healthcare, and architecture to bring 3D ideas to life, fast.

In this high-level overview, you'll watch Unity Studio's Car Review template transformed into an interactive building showcase, start to finish – the full workflow at speed, repurposed for an architectural experience instead of a car scene. Along the way you'll see how interactive 3D prototyping works in practice: an orbiting camera, clickable hotspots, and scene-wide lighting, all wired up with visual logic.

You'll learn how to do the following:
🔹 Choose the right template for an orbiting camera and clickable hotspots, and reuse the working pieces before repurposing the scene
 🔹 Dress and light the building for an afternoon mood, and place clickable points of interest
 🔹 Wire up two interactions with visual logic – then duplicate the pattern to build the rest

snippet.title: Opening Unity to everyone - one API, every role
snippet.description:
We’re opening the Editor to everyone!

For 20 years, the Unity Editor is where a whole generation of games has taken shape. But a game isn’t built in the Editor alone.

That’s why we’re building an API and set of services that open a Unity production to the tools, roles, and agents around it - no full Editor access required. Preview the real game, automate from the terminal, and use whatever tool fits the job. It’s built so every role on the team can contribute - whether you're an artist iterating on assets without wrestling with version control, or an engineer automating workflows from the command line, Unity plugs into your team's tools and your production pipeline, not the other way around

✅ Review the real game in context, together: Producers, artists, and QA review real game renders on the web or on device, not proxy screenshots. Share a link and feedback lands in live game context. 
✅ Build and automate your tools with AI: An API and CLI built for agents to validate assets, fix issues, submit for review, and trigger builds
✅ Bring in external collaborators, securely: Outsourced collaborators get role-based access. They work in their own tools, validate on device, and submit to your Version Control.

🔗 Now available in closed beta. Apply today: https://on.unity.com/ProductionPipeline

snippet.title: UNBEATABLE: How D-CELL makes 2D sprites pop in 3D environments
snippet.description:
Dive into the 8-year journey of D-CELL's breakthrough title, UNBEATABLE – a rhythm-based narrative action game made with Unity, where music is illegal and you do crimes.

Hear from Andrew Tsai, cofounder and creative director at D-CELL, who discusses the unique challenges and artistic decisions behind a game that started as a high school daydream and sold over 100,000 copies at launch eight years later.

This video explores:
✅ How the team tackled the complex challenge of audio precision in rhythm games, utilizing Unity and FMOD to sync game events and audio precisely in real time.
✅ Strategies for creating a dynamic, anime-inspired look by placing 2D character sprites into 3D environments.
✅ The team effort, commitment, and passion required to ship a massive project.

🔗 Play UNBEATABLE (Jamie Paige DLC out now): https://on.unity.com/PlayUNBEATABLE

snippet.title: Audi F1—Designing Livery with the Power of Unreal Engine | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
snippet.description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026, Audi AG gives a unique insight into their use of Unreal Engine to design the Audi F1 livery—and how they are pushing real-time workflows to the limit. 

The talk focuses on their Audi Visualization Unreal Solution platform—in-house tech that leverages the functionality of the Unreal Editor and exposes it to 3D artists in a way that centers on automotive visualization as the primary use case, while ensuring artists and visualization experts are not limited in what they can achieve. 

Watch to see a real-time, in-editor demo as well as technical deep dives into various Unreal Engine workflows, including how the team leverages Substrate—a node-based material authoring framework that replaces fixed shading models with a modular, layered system.

Find out more about using Unreal Engine for automotive here: unrealengine.com/uses/automotive

snippet.description:
This talk recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 explores how best to work with Unreal Engine and Clo/Marvelous Designer in combination, with a focus on MetaHuman technology. 

MetaHuman DNA imports have recently been incorporated into Clo software. We show how to create a MetaHuman using Unreal Engine, bring it into Clo, and then bring the clothing back into Unreal Engine. snippet.title: Leveraging Cultural Knowledge for Global UX
snippet.description:
Speaker: Chui Chui Tan

Expanding into international markets isn’t just about translating content or adjusting payment systems. Local cultures, political contexts, technological landscapes and social norms all shape how people perceive and interact with products or services.

In this talk, Chui Chui Tan will challenge traditional perspectives on cultural awareness in UX. She will show why it’s time for UX professionals to rethink how cultural factors impact global design, and how to translate that understanding into meaningful actions.

Through case studies and lessons from real-world international product launches, this talk will prompt attendees to reassess their approach to global UX, offering new frameworks for embedding cultural insights into every stage of product and business development.

snippet.title: AI is Transforming UX Research
snippet.description:
Speaker: John Whalen

I used to be skeptical of AI-powered tools and nervous about the sweeping changes they promise for our industry. But after interviewing over 25 AI research tool founders, testing nearly 100 AI-empowered solutions, and publishing our “AI vs Humans” study comparing traditional UX research with a human-plus-AI approach, I now see the transformative potential these tools offer.

In this talk, I reveal how advanced AI will reshape the way UX professionals work. Discover how AI moderation can dramatically accelerate and scale research, how synthetic users provide new avenues for creative experimentation, and how near-limitless insights generate empowers smarter, more informed design decisions.

I’ll provide a snapshot of the emerging roles and new skills that will define what we do. My hope is that you’ll leave not only better prepared, but also optimistic about the possibilities ahead. I look forward to learning from your unique perspectives as we navigate this transformative era together.

snippet.title: Design for Impact - Rally Your Team Around a Process that Drives Growth
snippet.description:
Speakers: Erin Weigel

Experimentation can be intimidating to non-data science folk. But Erin wants to get everyone excited about A/B testing.

In this talk, Erin shares the Conversion Design process. It centers A/B testing as a way to gather high-quality evidence to make highly informed decisions to improve your digital product design.

She also introduces the Good Experimental Design toolkit. These easy-to-follow templates usher teams through the logic needed to design trustworthy experiments that you can learn from so you can make things better—not just different.

snippet.title: Introduction to On-Set VFX Data
snippet.description:
The VES Technology Committee released their comprehensive guide for On-Set VFX Data, detailing the data types and capture methods overseen by production-side VFX teams and how they can best be used across a project. Designed to establish a common language between on‑set VFX, production, VFX facilities, and technology teams, to enable clearer communication, smoother handoffs, and better-aligned expectations so that every participant understands what information exists and how it can support their work.

The VES On-Set VFX Data Collection and Usage Guide was created for the VES Technology Committee by VES Award for Creative Excellence winning Visual Effects Supervisor Sheena Duggal, with contributions from VES Technology Committee Co-Chair, Open-Source Developer and former Disney Imagineer Sam Richards, TV Academy Governor, Virtual Production and Visual Effects Supervisor Jim Geduldick, and Visual Effects Supervisor Jake Morrison with technical support from Academy Software Foundation Technology Advisory Council member Jean‑Francois Panisset.

snippet.title: Building Production AI: The Future of VFX with Foundry and Griptape
snippet.description:
Recorded 5/19/26.  (ft Ben Lock, Jason Schleifer, Amaru Zeas-Siguenza) AI tools are everywhere, but how do they become part of an actual production pipeline? Join VES for a conversation with Griptape Creative Directors Jason Schleifer and Amaru Zeas, moderated by Ben Lock of Moonvalley, on how AI orchestration can power VFX pipelines. Griptape is designed to sit between models, tools, data, and users, helping teams build structured workflows that combine agents, APIs, automation, and human decision-making inside real production environments. As Foundry brings Griptape into its ecosystem, including Nuke integrations, this discussion will explore what the technology actually does, why Foundry acquired it, and what that may signal for the next phase of AI in professional VFX and animation workflows.

This discussion will ask some direct questions. What does Griptape actually do at a technical level? Why is orchestration becoming such an important layer in AI systems? What does it take to make AI workflows secure, repeatable, and usable in production? How do artists, TDs, developers, and production teams work together when AI becomes part of the pipeline rather than sitting outside it? And what might this acquisition signal about where AI-enabled VFX workflows are heading next?

snippet.title: VES Webinar: The VES Handbook of Virtual Production
snippet.description:
Edited by VFX Producer Susan Zwerman, VES, and renowned Visual Effects Supervisor Jeffrey A. Okun, VES, The VES Handbook of Virtual Production features real-world expertise gleaned from 82 experts in the world of Virtual Production in areas including VR, AR, MR, and XR technology, as well as detailed sections on interactive games, full animation and Unreal and Unity to provide real-time in-camera VFX. Additionally, the authors share their best methods, tips, tricks, and shortcuts developed as hands-on practitioners.
 
 The comprehensive VES Handbook of Virtual Production covers topics including: Visualization; VAD (Virtual Art Department); Volumetric Capture; How to Capture Environments; LED Stage Setup; LED Display; Software/Hardware for VP; Cameras and Camera Tracking; Color Management; External Lighting for the Volume; Challenges and Limitations of Shooting in a Volume; and a Virtual Production Glossary.

snippet.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King VFX | Weta Digital
snippet.description:
The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King is the epic conclusion to The Lord of Rings trilogy, and the result of almost a decade’s worth of creative and technological innovation. It encompasses ground-breaking technology and techniques. We used a multitude of sophisticated visual effects to create landscapes and creatures of unprecedented scale and complexity.
Our work on The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King won the Academy Award® for Best Visual Effects, and the BAFTA Award for Best Special Visual Effects.

Artists and Innovators in the World of Digital Entertainment.

snippet.title: Jungle Cruise VFX | Weta Digital
snippet.description:
Weta Digital’s contribution to Disney’s Jungle Cruise focused primarily on creating environments—including hundreds of kilometres of CG Amazon River, with mist, waterfalls and rapids—as well as the creatures that populate the jungle. We created and hand-animated Frank’s ever-loyal, and fully CG, pet jaguar Proxima, and crafted motion vignettes for the abundance of birds, bugs and monkeys that call the jungle home.

Artists and Innovators in the World of Digital Entertainment.

snippet.title: The Art of Virtual Production with Weta Digital
snippet.description:
Earlier in the year, our Executive Producer David Conley and two of our VFX Supervisors, Erik Winquist and Stephen Unterfranz, joined Shadow in the Cloud director Rosanne Liang on a panel for the DGA Virtual Production event. They had an open conversation about modern virtual production technology, including two projects with different LED workflows, and discussed in detail the learnings and challenges they experienced with some of our earlier LED virtual production projects.

Artists and Innovators in the World of Digital Entertainment.

This course was designed as a ground‑up introduction for artists coming from Cinema4D, Maya, Blender, or other 3D tools. We cover everything from project setup to real‑time rendering, including how to bring your C4D projects into Unreal Engine using FBX and other pipelines.

Description: 

Want to make your visual notes in Obsidian more engaging? In this video, I introduce the brand new "One-Click Icon Library" script for Obsidian! Previously, setting up an image library took a lot of manual configuration, but now you can search, select, and insert icons directly into your notes and mind maps with a single click or hotkey.
Stick around until the end for an awesome bonus feature: The Comic Strip Director! Contributed by Ivan from the Sketch Your Mind community, this script integrates seamlessly with the Comic Book Callout Editor to help you build out fun, visual comic strips right inside your vault.
Whether you're using PNGs, SVGs, or Excalidraw files, these tools will take your visual knowledge management to the next level. Go create something beautiful and don't forget to share it with us!

Description: 

Welcome to the latest Obsidian Excalidraw update! 🚀 June has been a massive month for the plugin. In this video, we dive into the new features in versions 2.24 and 2.25, including the plugin split (Excalidraw Core vs. Extras), an incredibly smooth new free-draw engine, reading modes for Markdown embeddables, and huge updates to the MindMap Builder.

Plus, we’ll look at powerful new community and official scripts, like the Comic Book Callout Editor, Ivan’s Color Scheme Manager, and Capture Note for visual daily note-taking.

Welcome to my new daily note-taking workflow! In this video, I'll show you how I've completely transformed my Personal Knowledge Management (PKM) and Getting Things Done (GTD) systems by ditching traditional walls of text for infinite, interconnected visual canvases.

Using Obsidian and Excalidraw, I've built a 100% visual daily journal setup. Watch as I demonstrate how to organize tasks, link project meetings, and capture ideas entirely in-context so you never lose track of an action item again. We also dive into the psychology of visual note-taking, touching on insights from James Clear and the LATCH framework for organizing information.

Finally, I’ll introduce the brand new "Capture Note" script for Excalidraw, which allows you to easily cross-link markdown documents and visual whiteboards directly from your daily notes.

Want to get your hands on the Demo Vault and access the full setup guide? Join the Sketch Your Mind community! We are an incredible group of visual thinkers and PKM enthusiasts. https://community.sketch-your-mind.com/welcome

---
Welcome to the massive Q1 2026 Obsidian-Excalidraw update! 🚀

In this video, I walk you through all the incredible new features, improvements, and UI tweaks added to the plugin over the past 4 months.
From game-changing spreadsheet integrations and Mermaid AI text-to-diagram capabilities to major upgrades for ExcaliAI, image handling, and presentation workflows, there is a lot to cover.

This recording is taken directly from the first half-hour of the inaugural Sketcher Mind community office hours. If you want to participate in amazing PKM discussions, Q&As, and master your visual note-taking skills, come join us!

⚡️ Highlighted Features in this Update:
• Integrations: Embed spreadsheets directly into your canvas via the Sheet Plus plugin and generate Mermaid diagrams via AI chat.
• ExcaliAI Updates: Keep track of token usage, mask API keys, and quickly touch up images and thumbnails.
• Workflow Enhancements: Inline link suggesters with frame support, a new toggle for View-Mode (perfect for presentations), and text-editing/lasso select UI improvements.
• Security Hardening: Important updates to keep your vault safe from malicious code in downloaded community templates or scripts.

If you found this video helpful, please hit the LIKE button, SUBSCRIBE for more Obsidian Excalidraw content, and leave a comment down below on which new feature is your favorite!

---

---

Let's have an honest, unscripted conversation about the future of Obsidian plugins.

Recently, Obsidian launched a new community site featuring security, quality, and maintenance reviews for plugins. While I completely understand and agree with the intent to protect users, the execution has placed a massive, unexpected burden on single-person hobby developers—including myself.

As the developer of Excalidraw (the most downloaded Obsidian plugin with over 6.1 million downloads), I was deeply upset to see how the automated scanner scores painted my life's work in an inaccurate and damaging light. In this video, I peel back the curtain to talk about the missing APIs forcing developers into workarounds, the massive gap between commercial expectations and hobbyist reality, and the harsh truth about community funding.

If we want the open-source Obsidian ecosystem to survive and thrive without burning out its creators, we need to talk about who pays the hidden costs.

👇 Join the Discussion:
If you want to dive deeper into this topic and all things visual PKM, join the Sketch Your Mind community: https://community.sketch-your-mind.com/welcome

☕ Support Excalidraw:
A massive thank you to the ~100 regular supporters who keep this project alive. If you get value out of Excalidraw and want to support its continued development, you can do so here: https://ko-fi.com/zsolt

#Obsidian #ObsidianMD #Excalidraw #PKM #OpenSource #Productivity #NoteTaking

💬 Meet on Mastodon: https://pkm.social/@zsviczian

-----

I believe that being a great storyteller is a real superpower. Whether you're in a boardroom or a Zoom call, a presentation is simply a story told at work. But what if you aren't a "natural" storyteller?

In this video, I share a visual "prosthetic" I built for myself to replace missing storytelling skills. Using the "South Park Secret" (learned from Trey Parker and Matt Stone) and Obsidian-Excalidraw, I’ll show you how to move away from boring "and then" sequences to dynamic narratives built on "but," "therefore," and "however."

We'll explore:
✅ The 5 types of visual connectors (Additive, Causal, Pivot, Reversal, and Loop).
✅ A practical walkthrough of "The Paradox of Focus" (based on Indistractable).
✅ How to use visual story cards to build narrative tension.
✅ A sneak peek into the Visual Thinking Workshop workflow.
If you struggle with logical thinking over emotional storytelling, this framework will help you visualize the "twists and turns" that keep an audience engaged.
